setting: Marseilles, 24 February 1815
keepInMind: France is ruled again by a Bourbon king, Louis XVIII. Napoleon abdicated in 1814 and lives in exile on the island of Elba, and many people still miss him. The story opens as a merchant ship comes into harbour.

setting: Marseilles, the same day
keepInMind: Morrel has all but promised young Dantès command of the Pharaon, which the supercargo Danglars watched with open resentment. Dantès stopped at Elba on his dead captain's orders, and Danglars saw him handed a letter as well as a packet.

setting: The Catalan village outside Marseilles, the same afternoon
keepInMind: Dantès has hurried off to see Mercédès. Caderousse has told Danglars that a strapping Catalan 'cousin' always walks with her, and the two men have settled into the tavern arbour at La Réserve to wait for news.

setting: The arbour at La Réserve, moments later
keepInMind: Fernand has been refused by Mercédès and has just watched her walk off with Dantès. Danglars has heard that Dantès must go to Paris to deliver 'the letter which the grand marshal gave him', and says it gives him an idea.

setting: La Réserve, the next day
keepInMind: Danglars wrote a denunciation of Dantès with his left hand and tossed it, crumpled, into a corner, but Fernand picked it up and hurried off toward the city. Caderousse was too drunk to remember clearly.

setting: Marseilles, the same day, at a royalist betrothal feast in an aristocratic mansion
keepInMind: Dantès has been arrested at his wedding feast as a Bonapartist agent. Morrel has gone to plead with the deputy prosecutor, M. de Villefort.

setting: Marseilles, that afternoon
keepInMind: Villefort is about to marry into a fiercely royalist family, but his own father, the former Girondin and imperial senator Noirtier, is a Bonapartist whose name he has dropped. Renée begged him to be merciful, and the denunciation claims that Dantès carries a letter for Paris.

setting: Marseilles, that evening
keepInMind: Villefort burned the Elba letter, which was addressed to his own father, and made Dantès swear never to mention it, promising he would be held only until evening. Alone, Villefort told himself that the letter could make his fortune.

setting: The Saint-Méran house, the same evening
keepInMind: We go back a few hours to the moment Villefort left Dantès and hurried to his betrothed's house with a plan of his own.

setting: Paris: the king's private study in the Tuileries palace
keepInMind: Villefort is racing to Paris with Salvieux's letter of introduction, hoping to be the first to warn the king of a plot from Elba and so make his fortune. The Elba letter he burned was addressed to his own father.

setting: The Tuileries, a moment later
keepInMind: Villefort has just told Louis XVIII that Napoleon is arming ships on Elba, and the king brushed off the danger. Dandré, the minister of police, who had called the rumours nonsense, has appeared at the door looking pale. The police are also investigating a Bonapartist club in the Rue Saint-Jacques.

setting: Villefort's Paris hotel, the same day
keepInMind: The police are hunting a dark man of about fifty, in a blue frock-coat with black whiskers, over General Quesnel's death. They lost him near the Rue Coq-Héron, the street on the Elba letter. That man has just walked into Villefort's room: it is his father, Noirtier.

setting: Marseilles, spring 1815 and the months that follow
keepInMind: Noirtier predicted that Napoleon would reach Paris without a shot fired, and told his son to go home and keep quiet. Villefort alone knows why Dantès really vanished.

setting: The Château d'If, a year after the king's second restoration
keepInMind: Dantès threatened his jailer and was thrown into a lower dungeon 'with the madmen'. The jailer had warned him about an abbé who went mad offering the governor millions for his freedom.

setting: The Château d'If, the years that follow
keepInMind: The inspector's visit came to nothing: a note added to Dantès's file branded him a dangerous Bonapartist. Under a new governor he is known only as Number 34. The 'mad' Abbé Faria, who offers millions for his release, is Number 27.

setting: Dantès's cell
keepInMind: After four or five years without hearing any voice but his jailer's, Dantès has just seen his fellow tunneller climb up into his cell.

setting: The tunnel to the abbé's cell
keepInMind: Faria has told Dantès that he made his own pens, ink and paper and wrote a whole treatise in prison, and he is now taking him through the tunnel to see.

setting: The Château d'If, the next morning
keepInMind: Faria survived a terrible seizure but is now partly paralysed. He said he had something of the greatest importance to tell Dantès. Remember that the prison thinks him mad because he talks of a hidden treasure.

setting: The Château d'If
keepInMind: Faria has shared Cardinal Spada's secret, a treasure buried on the island of Monte Cristo, and named Dantès his heir. He has also warned that a third attack would kill him or leave him helpless.

setting: Faria's cell, that day
keepInMind: Faria is dead. His body has been sewn into a sack, and the governor has ordered it taken out at about ten or eleven tonight. No one knows of the tunnel.

setting: The sea off the Château d'If, that night
keepInMind: Dantès took Faria's place in the sack. Instead of burying him, the grave-diggers hurled him into the sea with a cannonball tied to his feet. He still has Faria's knife.

setting: Aboard the Genoese tartan La Jeune Amélie, bound for Leghorn, late February 1829
keepInMind: Dantès has passed himself off as a shipwrecked Maltese sailor on a vessel that is plainly a smuggler. It is fourteen years to the day since his arrest. He has renewed his vow of vengeance on Danglars, Fernand and Villefort.

setting: Leghorn, then at sea
keepInMind: The smugglers have picked the deserted island of Monte Cristo for their next rendezvous. Remember Spada's directions: count twenty rocks from the small creek to the east; there are two openings, and the treasure lies in the farthest angle of the second.

setting: The island of Monte Cristo, 1829
keepInMind: Dantès faked a bad fall so the smugglers would leave him alone on Monte Cristo. He is following the carved marks on the rocks, guided by Faria's half-burnt letter, which says Cardinal Spada's treasure lies in the farthest angle of the second opening.

setting: Monte Cristo, 1829
keepInMind: Dantès is now the owner of Cardinal Spada's enormous treasure, but he is still only a poor sailor in the smugglers' eyes, and they are due back for him in about six days. In fourteen years he has had no word of his father or of Mercédès.

setting: A roadside inn between Beaucaire and Bellegarde, in the south of France
keepInMind: In Marseilles, Dantès (travelling as the Englishman Lord Wilmore) learned that Caderousse fell on hard times and now keeps a small inn on this road. Fourteen years ago Caderousse was the drunken witness when Danglars wrote the denunciation, and he kept silent at the arrest.

returning.reminder: Dantès' envious neighbour, a tailor, who saw the denunciation written and said nothing.

setting: The same roadside inn, moments later
keepInMind: The abbé has shown Caderousse a diamond worth fifty thousand francs, said to be Dantès' bequest to his old friends. Tempted, Caderousse has bolted the door to tell everything, against his wife's warnings.

setting: Marseilles, 1829
keepInMind: Caderousse named Danglars and Fernand as the authors of the denunciation, but could say nothing about Villefort's part. He also said that Morrel's firm is close to ruin, with all its hopes on the Pharaon's return from India, and the abbé took Morrel's old red silk purse in exchange for the diamond.

setting: Marseilles, the offices of Morrel & Son
keepInMind: A clerk from the Roman bank Thomson & French has just bought up the 200,000 francs Morrel owes M. de Boville, half of it due this month. Caderousse said Morrel's last hope is the Pharaon, now overdue from India.

returning.reminder: Owner of the Pharaon and Dantès' kind old employer, who pleaded for him.

setting: Marseilles, summer 1829
keepInMind: The Pharaon is lost, and Morrel's bills for 287,500 francs now fall due on 5 September at eleven o'clock. The Thomson & French clerk told Julie that one day she will get a letter signed 'Sinbad the Sailor', and made her swear to obey it.

setting: Florence and the Tuscan coast, early 1838, about nine years later
keepInMind: Dantès left Marseilles a fabulously rich man, vowing that he was done with rewarding the good and would now punish the wicked. Caderousse said Fernand has become the Count de Morcerf, husband of Mercédès and father of a son, Albert. We now meet two young Parisian aristocrats.

returning.reminder: Son of Mercédès and Fernand, now Count de Morcerf; Caderousse mentioned 'little Albert'.

setting: The island of Monte Cristo, the next morning
keepInMind: Franz was led blindfold into an underground palace, dined there with a mysterious host who calls himself 'Sinbad the Sailor', took hashish and sank into a wild dream. Meanwhile Albert is waiting for him in Rome for the Carnival.

setting: Rome, the Hôtel de Londres, a few days before Carnival
keepInMind: Franz and Albert have rooms at Signor Pastrini's crowded hotel, but no carriage can be found. The rest of their floor is taken by a very rich traveller, perhaps Sicilian or Maltese. Franz promised his sailors to say nothing about his night on Monte Cristo.

setting: Rome, by moonlight
keepInMind: Pastrini's story of Luigi Vampa, the shepherd boy who became a bandit chief, included a traveller who called himself 'Sinbad the Sailor', and Franz was startled to hear the name. The friends are now on their way to the Colosseum, taking the streets rather than the bandit-haunted road outside the walls.

setting: Rome, 23 February, the first day of Carnival
keepInMind: Franz now knows that their neighbour, the Count of Monte Cristo, is his host from the island, the man he saw at the opera, and the cloaked figure at the Colosseum. There he heard the man promise a bandit to save the condemned Peppino and arrange a signal: a white damask with a red cross at the middle window of the Rospoli palace.

setting: Rome, the Carnival
keepInMind: From the count's window, Franz and Albert watched Peppino pardoned at the foot of the scaffold and the murderer Andrea put to death, with the count looking on in grim triumph. Masked revelry follows straight after the executions.

setting: Rome, the last night of Carnival
keepInMind: Albert vanished into the crowd arm in arm with his masked peasant beauty just as the Carnival's candles went out, leaving Franz alone in the dark. Both friends are expected that night at the Duke of Bracciano's ball, along with the Countess G——.

setting: Rome, the morning after Albert's release
keepInMind: The Count of Monte Cristo has just talked Luigi Vampa into freeing Albert without ransom. Franz, who met the same man as 'Sinbad' on Monte Cristo and overheard him at the Colosseum, saw him shudder as he shook Albert's hand.

setting: Paris, 21 May 1838: three months later
keepInMind: In Rome the Count promised to call on Albert at No. 27 Rue du Helder on 21 May at exactly half-past ten. Albert's father has summoned him home to arrange a marriage.

setting: Albert's rooms, Rue du Helder, the same morning
keepInMind: Albert's breakfast guests, Debray and Beauchamp, are waiting, and Albert has two more expected, among them his mysterious guest from Rome. Nobody but Albert believes the Count will turn up on time.

returning.reminder: Morrel's son, the upright young officer nicknamed 'the stoic'

setting: Albert's pavilion and his parents' house
keepInMind: Remember what Caderousse told the abbé: Fernand rose to become the Count de Morcerf, a rich general, and married Mercédès. Albert de Morcerf is their son, and he has promised to introduce the Count to his parents.

returning.reminder: Dantès' Catalan fiancée, who later married Fernand
Mercédès' jealous cousin who posted the denunciation; now Count de Morcerf

setting: The Count's new house on the Champs-Élysées
keepInMind: Ali went ahead to find and furnish a Paris house. The Count told the breakfast party that his steward is a Corsican who may once have been mixed up in 'a stab with a knife'.

returning.reminder: The Count's Corsican steward from Rome, a former soldier and smuggler

setting: Auteuil, just outside Paris, that evening
keepInMind: The Count has bought a country house at Auteuil without seeing it. Bertuccio went white at the address and begged him to buy elsewhere, but must now show him round it tonight.

setting: The garden at Auteuil, at night; Bertuccio's story begins in 1815
keepInMind: Bertuccio has admitted that he stabbed M. de Villefort in this garden as an act of vendetta, and that Villefort had just buried something there. Think back to 1815: Napoleon's Hundred Days, Waterloo, and the royalist revenge that followed.

setting: Bertuccio's story continues: an inn near Beaucaire, June 1829
keepInMind: Hidden in the shed, Bertuccio watched Caderousse and La Carconte sell the abbé's diamond to the jeweller Joannes for 45,000 francs. A violent storm has just driven the jeweller back to spend the night at the inn.

setting: The Count's house in Paris, the next afternoon
keepInMind: The Count's first engraved card went to Baron Danglars, on whom he holds credit through Thomson & French. Albert is expected to marry Danglars' daughter Eugénie.

returning.reminder: Wrote the denunciation that jailed Dantès; now a rich Paris banker and baron

setting: Baron Danglars' house in the Chaussée d'Antin
keepInMind: The Count has had Danglars' prized horses bought at double the price and harnessed to his own carriage, then driven to the banker's house to be introduced to the baroness. Lucien Debray is with her.

setting: The Count's house on the Champs-Élysées
keepInMind: Ali saved Madame de Villefort and her son from the runaway horses, and Villefort has come in person to give thanks. In Bertuccio's story, Villefort survived the stabbing in the Auteuil garden.

returning.reminder: Marseilles prosecutor who buried Dantès in the Château d'If; now powerful in Paris

setting: Haydée's apartments in the Count's house
keepInMind: Haydée, the Count's Greek companion from Rome, arrived secretly at midnight and lives in hidden rooms. The Count calls her his slave, though under French law any slave on French soil is free. He is also about to visit old friends in the Rue Meslay.

setting: The Morrels' house, Rue Meslay, Paris
keepInMind: Maximilian invited the Count to meet his sister Julie and her husband Emmanuel. Nine years ago Morrel was saved at the last moment by the red silk purse and a letter signed 'Sinbad the Sailor'.

returning.reminder: Morrel's daughter, who found the red purse that saved her father
The loyal young clerk who loved Julie and stayed with the failing firm
Morrel & Son's devoted one-eyed cashier
Old sailor who survived the Pharaon's wreck

setting: Behind a grand house in the Faubourg Saint-Honoré, on a warm spring evening
keepInMind: Remember the Villefort household: the stern prosecutor, his second wife Héloïse and their spoiled son Edward, and Valentine, his daughter by his first marriage, who cares for her paralyzed grandfather Noirtier.

setting: Madame de Villefort's drawing room
keepInMind: The Count is returning Villefort's visit. When he revived Edward with a single drop from a blood-red phial, Madame de Villefort took a long look at his casket of bottles.

setting: The Paris Opéra, at a performance of Robert le Diable
keepInMind: The Count said he would take a Greek princess to the opera. Albert's thoughts are on his arranged match with Eugénie Danglars. In Rome a witty Venetian countess nicknamed the Count 'Lord Ruthven', after a famous fictional vampire.

returning.reminder: Witty Venetian countess in Rome who decided the pale Count was a vampire

setting: The Count's house on the Champs-Élysées, a few days later
keepInMind: Albert's marriage to Eugénie Danglars is being pushed forward, though he is unenthusiastic. At the Opéra, Haydée accused the Count de Morcerf of selling her father to the Turks. Debray is close to Madame Danglars.

setting: Paris, the count's house on the Champs-Élysées, 1838
keepInMind: The count turned down Albert's invitation by saying he was expecting an Italian, Major Cavalcanti, whose son is also coming to Paris. He has promised to look after the young Andrea as he makes his entry into Paris society.

setting: The count's house, a few minutes later
keepInMind: The count has just coached 'Major Cavalcanti' through a ready-made family history and left him waiting to meet his 'lost son'. The major barely knew his own story; the count supplied every detail and even the papers.

setting: Paris, the gate at the bottom of the Villefort garden
keepInMind: Maximilian Morrel and Valentine de Villefort meet in secret through a boarded-up gate in her family's garden (ch 51). She is engaged, against her wishes, to Albert's friend Franz d'Épinay, who is still in Italy.

setting: The Villefort house, the same afternoon
keepInMind: Valentine's grandfather Noirtier, once a fiery Jacobin and Bonapartist conspirator, is now paralysed and speechless; she is the one person he loves. Villefort is determined to marry her to Franz d'Épinay.

returning.reminder: Villefort's father: an old revolutionary conspirator, now paralysed and devoted to Valentine.

setting: Noirtier's rooms in the Villefort house, Paris, moments later
keepInMind: Furious at the news of Valentine's engagement to Franz, Noirtier made her understand that he wants a notary. Over Villefort's objections, the loyal servant Barrois has gone to fetch one.

setting: The Villefort house, the same day
keepInMind: Noirtier has just dictated a will: if Valentine marries Franz d'Épinay, his 900,000 francs will go to the poor rather than to the family. He and Franz's father were bitter political enemies.

setting: South of Paris, on the road to Orléans, the next morning
keepInMind: Leaving the Villeforts, the count said he was off to look at a telegraph tower on the Spanish line. Danglars speculates heavily on the Bourse, and Madame Danglars, a close friend of the minister's secretary Debray, dabbles there too.

setting: The count's house at Auteuil, the Saturday of his dinner
keepInMind: The Auteuil house once belonged to Villefort's in-laws, the Saint-Mérans. Bertuccio told the count what he witnessed in its garden years ago: a pregnant woman waiting in the house, and a man burying a box under the trees, whom Bertuccio stabbed in vendetta.

returning.reminder: The count's Corsican steward, haunted by his vendetta killing in the Auteuil garden.

setting: Auteuil, the dinner party
keepInMind: Peering at the guests, Bertuccio recognized Madame Danglars as the woman from the garden, Villefort as the man he thought he had killed, and 'Andrea Cavalcanti' as Benedetto, the boy he raised.

setting: Auteuil, as the guests leave
keepInMind: At dinner the count showed his guests the red bedroom and its hidden staircase and announced that a newborn's skeleton had been dug up in the garden. Madame Danglars fainted, and Villefort whispered that he must see her the next day.

setting: Paris, that night: the Danglars house
keepInMind: Debray rode back from Auteuil with the Villeforts' carriage, which is taking Madame Danglars home. Danglars has just lost heavily by selling his Spanish bonds on the false telegraph news (ch 61).

setting: Paris, the next day
keepInMind: Danglars has confronted his wife over his Spanish losses and named her lovers, Villefort among them. Remember that the Comte de Morcerf, Albert's father, is Fernand, the Catalan fisherman who helped betray Edmond, and who once served Ali Pasha (ch 53).

setting: Paris, the same morning: the Palais de Justice
keepInMind: At the dinner Villefort asked Madame Danglars to meet him at his office. Recall Bertuccio's story (ch 44): after stabbing the man in the Auteuil garden, he dug up the buried box and found the baby inside still alive.

setting: Paris: the Rue du Helder and the count's house, the same day
keepInMind: Albert and his mother left Paris for the seaside to avoid meeting Danglars at the Auteuil dinner. Danglars now prefers Andrea Cavalcanti to Albert for Eugénie, and on the count's hint has written to Yanina about Morcerf's past.

returning.reminder: Albert's mother, the Countess de Morcerf: once Edmond's fiancée in Marseilles.

setting: Paris
keepInMind: Villefort swore to Madame Danglars that within a week he would find out who the Count of Monte Cristo really is. The count says the Cavalcantis came to him through two acquaintances: the Abbé Busoni and an eccentric Englishman, Lord Wilmore.

returning.reminder: Former inspector of prisons who showed the 'Englishman' Dantès' prison records.

setting: The Morcerfs' house, a hot Saturday night in July
keepInMind: Albert told the count that his mother particularly wanted him at their ball. At the opera, Haydée recognized the Comte de Morcerf as the man who betrayed her father (ch 53). Villefort's inquiries produced a harmless official story about the count.

setting: The Morcerfs' garden, during the ball
keepInMind: Mercédès noticed that the count has refused all food and drink under her husband's roof. She has just taken his arm to lead the guests out into the garden.

setting: The Villefort house, the same night
keepInMind: News reached the ball that the Marquis de Saint-Méran, Valentine's grandfather, had died on the road to Paris, where he was coming to hurry on her marriage to Franz. Villefort has been brooding over who could know his Auteuil secret.

returning.reminder: Renée's mother and Valentine's grandmother: proud, stern and fiercely royalist.

setting: The gate at the bottom of the Villefort garden
keepInMind: Feverish with grief, Madame de Saint-Méran demands that Valentine marry Franz at once and has sent for a notary. While Dr d'Avrigny examined her grandmother, Valentine went down to the garden and heard Maximilian calling her.

setting: Paris, two days later
keepInMind: Madame de Saint-Méran has died. Dr d'Avrigny privately told Villefort he believes she was poisoned, and they agreed to keep silent. Noirtier made Maximilian swear to wait, promising that the marriage contract would not be signed.

returning.reminder: Albert's sceptical journalist friend, who writes for an opposition newspaper.

setting: Noirtier's room, moments later
keepInMind: Franz's father, General d'Épinay (born de Quesnel), was a royalist killed in 1815 after leaving a Bonapartist club, and the crime was never solved. Noirtier hated him, and has summoned Franz just as the contract was about to be signed.

setting: Paris, a couple of weeks later
keepInMind: Danglars has been warming to Andrea as a husband for Eugénie and cooling toward Albert. On the count's suggestion he wrote to his correspondent at Yanina to ask what part Fernand Mondego played in Ali Pasha's downfall.

setting: Paris: the count’s house on the Champs-Élysées, late in the evening
keepInMind: Danglars has asked the count to press the Morcerfs for a decision on Albert’s marriage to Eugénie, and has just had news from Greece about ‘Fernand and Yanina’. The count lives with a beautiful Greek girl, Haydée, whom few people have ever met.

returning.reminder: The count’s mute Nubian servant, utterly devoted to him.

setting: Paris: the same day
keepInMind: In front of Villefort, Noirtier has just shown Franz that Franz’s father died in a fair duel in 1815 and that Noirtier himself was his opponent. Separately, Danglars wrote to Yanina asking about Fernand’s past, and Albert has promised the count never to tell Haydée that his father served hers.

setting: Paris: the Villefort house in the Faubourg Saint-Honoré, a few days later
keepInMind: Franz has broken off the engagement, and Noirtier has made Valentine his heir on condition that she never leaves him. Remember Dr. d’Avrigny’s secret warning to Villefort after Madame de Saint-Méran’s death: he believes she was poisoned.

setting: The Villefort house, moments later
keepInMind: Barrois has just died after drinking from Noirtier’s lemonade, which Valentine had handed to him. D’Avrigny’s syrup-of-violets test proved it was poisoned, he says with the same poison that killed Madame de Saint-Méran.

setting: Paris: the evening Morcerf left Danglars’ house
keepInMind: Danglars has put off Morcerf’s proposal for Albert, and Andrea Cavalcanti has been courting Eugénie with Danglars’ encouragement. Ever since the dinner at Auteuil, Andrea has been paying Caderousse a monthly allowance to stay quiet.

returning.reminder: Escaped convict who knew Andrea in prison as Benedetto; now blackmailing him.

setting: Auteuil and the Champs-Élysées: the next day and night
keepInMind: Andrea drew Caderousse a plan of the count’s house, described the secretaire in the dressing-room, and told him the count would spend this night at Auteuil.

returning.reminder: The count’s devoted Corsican steward, who runs his households and errands.

setting: The count’s house on the Champs-Élysées, straight afterwards
keepInMind: Caught in the act by the count disguised as the Abbé Busoni, Caderousse was made to write a letter exposing Andrea and was let go by the window. Outside the garden wall, a man waiting in the shadows stabbed him three times.

setting: Paris: the following three weeks
keepInMind: Before he died, Caderousse signed a statement naming Benedetto, alias Andrea Cavalcanti, as his murderer, and the count revealed his true identity to him. Beauchamp has been away almost all of the three weeks he asked for before answering Albert’s challenge over the Yanina paragraph.

setting: Paris: the count’s house on the Champs-Élysées
keepInMind: Beauchamp has brought back proof from Yanina that Fernand Mondego, Albert’s father, betrayed Ali Pasha. Albert burned the papers, and the two friends have decided to call on the count. The count’s steward has a house and boat ready on the Normandy coast.

setting: Paris: Beauchamp’s rooms, early the next morning
keepInMind: A second newspaper, a pro-government one, has openly named the Count of Morcerf as the French officer who betrayed Yanina. Albert has ridden through the night from Normandy to find Beauchamp.

setting: Paris: Beauchamp’s rooms, the same morning
keepInMind: Beauchamp is finishing his account of the inquiry in the Chamber of Peers, which found Albert’s father guilty after Haydée gave evidence. Remember that Danglars wrote to Yanina for news of Fernand just before he turned down Morcerf’s proposal.

setting: Paris: outside Danglars’ house, the same day
keepInMind: Danglars has told Albert it was the count who advised him to write to Yanina. Albert now believes the count planned his father’s ruin from the start, and Beauchamp agrees that the count owes him an explanation.

returning.reminder: Maximilian’s sister, Morrel the shipowner’s daughter, happily married to Emmanuel.
Julie’s husband, the former Morrel clerk; Maximilian’s brother-in-law.

setting: The count’s house, that night after the Opera
keepInMind: At the Opera Albert publicly challenged the count to a duel with pistols, at eight next morning in the Bois de Vincennes. The count told Maximilian he would kill Albert. Earlier, Mercédès had ordered a servant to follow her son wherever he went.

setting: The count’s house, through the night and into the morning
keepInMind: Mercédès called him Edmond and begged for her son’s life. The count promised that Albert would live, which, he told her, means letting Albert kill him in the duel.

setting: The dueling ground in the Bois de Vincennes, then the Morcerf house
keepInMind: Instead of fighting, Albert publicly apologized and declared the count had been right to avenge himself on Albert’s father. The count saw Mercédès’s hand in it: she must have told her son the truth.

setting: Paris: the same morning
keepInMind: Albert and Mercédès are leaving the Morcerf house for good, giving up its name and fortune. They have accepted the count’s small gift of the money he once buried for Mercédès. Riding home, Albert glimpsed his father watching from behind a curtain.

setting: The Villefort house: the same morning
keepInMind: After Barrois’s death, d’Avrigny accused Valentine of the poisonings and said he would never come to the house again. Villefort refused to believe him and kept the secret, and all the servants left. Noirtier means to move out and take Valentine with him, and he has blessed her future with Maximilian.

returning.reminder: Villefort’s daughter, Noirtier’s heir, secretly engaged to Maximilian; the doctor suspects her.
Valentine’s paralysed grandfather, who speaks with his eyes; Barrois drank his poisoned lemonade.

setting: Paris: moments later
keepInMind: Valentine collapsed in front of Maximilian and Noirtier after drinking water that tasted bitter. For some time she had been taking spoonfuls of Noirtier’s medicine on his orders. That same morning the count told Maximilian to come to him if he ever needed help.

returning.reminder: The Villeforts’ doctor, who proved Barrois was poisoned and suspects Valentine.

setting: Danglars’ house: earlier that same morning
keepInMind: The story steps back a few hours, to before the Danglars ladies’ visit. Eugénie has never wanted a husband; she dreams of an artist’s independent life with her friend Louise d’Armilly. Danglars has suffered heavy losses in recent months.

setting: Paris: three days later, the evening the marriage contract is to be signed
keepInMind: Eugénie has agreed to sign the contract with Andrea on condition that she stays free in her own person. The police are still searching for Caderousse’s murderer.

setting: Danglars’ house: minutes after the contract scene
keepInMind: The police burst in to arrest Andrea for Caderousse’s murder, but he had already slipped away. Louise d’Armilly has letters of introduction from the count for theatres in Italy.

setting: Paris and the road north: the same night
keepInMind: Andrea vanished from the contract party moments before the police arrived. Eugénie, dressed as a young man, and Louise have left Paris by post-chaise for Belgium.

setting: Paris, the night of the contract scandal and the next morning
keepInMind: Andrea Cavalcanti has been exposed as Benedetto, an escaped convict wanted for Caderousse’s murder, and Eugénie has secretly fled. Remember what the reader knows and they do not: Andrea is the baby Villefort buried at Auteuil, his son by Madame Danglars.

setting: Villefort’s house in Paris: Valentine’s sickroom
keepInMind: Valentine collapsed after drinking poisoned water; Noirtier had been quietly building up her resistance with his own medicine. Monte Cristo promised Maximilian she would not die, and the Abbé Busoni, the count in another of his guises, has rented the house next door.

setting: Valentine’s room, at midnight
keepInMind: The count, who has been secretly swapping Valentine’s poisoned drinks for safe ones, has told her to lie still and pretend to sleep, so that she can see for herself who comes.

setting: Valentine’s room, later that night
keepInMind: Valentine has seen her stepmother pour poison into her glass and heard the motive: her fortune would pass, through her father, to little Edward. She has promised to put herself entirely in the count’s hands.

setting: Villefort’s house, the same morning
keepInMind: Valentine has been found dead and d’Avrigny has detected poison in her glass. Maximilian, whose love her father knew nothing of, arrived to hear the word “Dead!” Recall that he once overheard d’Avrigny warn Villefort, in the garden, that someone in the house was a poisoner.

setting: Paris, the morning of Valentine’s funeral
keepInMind: Villefort has sworn a terrible revenge within three days, and the Abbé Busoni is keeping watch over Valentine with Noirtier. Recall too that Danglars, close to ruin, holds millions belonging to the Paris charities, and that Monte Cristo has unlimited credit at his bank.

setting: Paris: the cemetery of Père-Lachaise
keepInMind: Maximilian left Valentine’s deathbed in despair, feeling the count had broken his promise that she would live. Neither he nor Monte Cristo appeared at the funeral reception.

returning.reminder: Old quartermaster of the Pharaon, now the Morrel family’s gardener.

setting: Paris: a modest house in the Rue Saint-Germain-des-Prés
keepInMind: Danglars was quietly preparing to flee after handing the count the hospitals’ five million. Madame Danglars and Debray have long speculated together on the Bourse. Albert and Mercédès gave up the Morcerf name and fortune; the count told Mercédès of a small sum he buried for her in Marseilles.

returning.reminder: Dantès’ first love, who left Morcerf’s house and fortune; she knows the count is Edmond.
Mercédès’ son, who renounced his father’s name and fortune after Morcerf’s disgrace.

setting: La Force prison, Paris
keepInMind: Andrea, alias Benedetto, was arrested at Compiègne. As he was taken he told Eugénie that “one has friends”: he is convinced a powerful secret patron has been behind his whole rise.

returning.reminder: The count’s Corsican steward, who saved the baby Benedetto and helped raise him.

setting: Villefort’s house, in the days before Benedetto’s trial
keepInMind: Noirtier named Valentine’s murderer to Villefort alone, and Villefort swore that the culprit would be punished sooner than the law could manage. Bertuccio has promised to return and tell Benedetto who his father is.

setting: The Palais de Justice, Paris, on a bright September day
keepInMind: That morning Villefort accused his wife of four murders and ordered her to be dead before he came home from court. He has gone to prosecute Benedetto with no idea that the accused is his own son.

setting: The assize court, Paris
keepInMind: Bertuccio has visited Benedetto a second time, as promised, to tell him his father’s name. In the crowd, Beauchamp is sure a veiled lady is Madame Danglars.

setting: Paris, leaving the Palais de Justice
keepInMind: Before he left for court, Villefort told his wife to take her own poison before he returned, or he would arrest her with his own hands. The Abbé Busoni has stayed close to Noirtier since Valentine’s death.

setting: Paris: the Morrels’ home in the Rue Meslay
keepInMind: Monte Cristo has told Maximilian that they leave Paris tomorrow. Maximilian has sworn not to take his life for one month, until 5 October, and is now in the count’s keeping.

setting: Marseilles
keepInMind: Since Edward’s death the count has begun, for the first time, to doubt his right to the vengeance he has taken. He has just said farewell to Mercédès, and Maximilian has gone to weep at his father’s grave.

setting: Italy: the post road from Florence to Rome
keepInMind: Danglars fled Paris with the count’s receipt for over five million francs, payable by the bank of Thomson & French in Rome. The count, for his part, told the Morrels he had to be in Rome within five days.

returning.reminder: Roman innkeeper who hosted Franz and Albert at Carnival time.
Vampa’s man, whom the count saved from the scaffold in Rome.
Roman bandit chief who kidnapped Albert, and who obeys the count.

setting: A cell in the catacombs of Saint Sebastian, outside Rome
keepInMind: Danglars is the prisoner of Vampa’s bandits. Remembering that Albert was ransomed for 4,000 crowns, he expects to buy his freedom cheaply and keep the rest of his five million.

setting: The bandits’ catacombs outside Rome
keepInMind: The bandits have left Danglars his money but charge 100,000 francs for a chicken, paid by drafts on Thomson & French. He has already signed the first.

setting: The Mediterranean, off the island of Monte Cristo: 5 October, evening
keepInMind: A month ago Monte Cristo swore that if Maximilian was still not consoled by 5 October, he would set pistols and a gentle poison before him himself. He arranged for the yacht Eurus to bring Maximilian from Bastia to meet him on the island.

returning.reminder: Corsican sailor who pulled the escaped Dantès from the sea; loyal to him ever since.
